tut1a: The goal of LumineBlock is to fit pieces onto the board and clear lines and columns to score as many points as possible.
tut1b: The board is a square grid of cells. You choose the size on the home screen: from 5×5 up to 12×12.
tut1c: Pieces are shapes made of colorful blocks. They cannot be rotated.
tut1d: The piece tray below the board displays 3 pieces. When you place all three, 3 new ones arrive.
tut1e: You only score points by completing and clearing rows or columns.
tut2a: Check the available pieces at the bottom.
tut2c: Tap and drag it with your finger without letting go.
tut2d: Move it over an empty area of the board. A shadow shows where it will be placed.
tut2f: The board and your score update immediately.
tut2Rule: The piece must fit completely: it cannot go outside the board or overlap occupied cells. If the placement is invalid, the shadow turns red and the piece returns to the tray.
tut3a: Fill all the cells in a horizontal line to clear it.
tut3b: Fill all the cells in a vertical column to clear it.
tut3c: Completed lines and columns glow and disappear, clearing their cells again. Other blocks do not move.
tut3d: A single piece can complete multiple lines and columns at once: all of them are cleared together.
tut3e: Cleared cells make room for upcoming pieces, including those that previously had no space.
tut4a: Simply placing a piece does not award points.
tut4b: Each completed and cleared horizontal row or vertical column is worth 10 points.
tut4c: Simultaneous clears add 10 points per row or column: 1 = 10, 2 = 20, 3 = 30. A row and a column together are worth 20 points.
tut4d: Each clear is celebrated with a message: Nice! (1), Excellent! (2), Incredible! (3), Fantastic! (4), and Perfect! (5 or more). Messages do not award extra points.
tut4e: Your high score is automatically updated whenever the current game's score surpasses it.
tut5a: Sometimes a piece won't fit anywhere on the board. It becomes temporarily unavailable: dimmed and unlit.
tut5b: Unavailable pieces cannot be selected, dragged, or placed.
tut5c: When lines or columns are cleared and space opens up, the piece automatically becomes available again.
tut6a: The game ends automatically when none of the available pieces have a valid position on the board.
tut6b: On the game over screen, you see your final score and can choose:
tut6c: Restart: starts a new game with a clean board and fresh pieces.
tut6d: Back to home: returns to the home screen.
tut6e: Your personal record and statistics are always saved.
tip1: Plan where each piece will go before releasing it.
tip2: Avoid filling the board without a strategy.
tip3: Examine all three pieces before making a move.
tip4: Always aim to complete lines and columns.
tip5: Keep open spaces for larger pieces, such as the 3×3 square.
tip6: Set up moves that clear multiple rows and columns at once.
tip7: Choose a board size that suits your playstyle: smaller boards are fast-paced, while larger ones offer more freedom.
